content:
@Dave Register @Pavel Kalian

We should IMHO make some decision: should we use wx 3.3 for 5.16 windows builds or not?

There are good arguments for using 3.3 on Windows. I'm particularly concerned about all menu colour stuff like #5466 which will have a new context when we move to 3.3 and the related windows dark mode. It would also mean much more common code paths for this stuff which has annoying details.

There is also a question about the wisdom about releasing win64 using wxw 3.2, just to replace it with 3.3/3.4 months later. Perhaps better to jump on 3.3 directly for at least win64?

That said, moving to 3.3 will affect plugins, obscure compilation errors typically when plugins tries to iterate over API wxList lists.
It seems that the wxList 3.3 incompatibilities basically are about how the plugins use the API, not the API as such.

Thoughts?

See also #5081 and #5466

I doubt wxwidgets 3.4 will make it for Debian forky, so we should probably plan for using 3.2 in 5.16 Linux builds
I would switch to wx3.3. Our primary Win platform will be x64, so new plugin builds are inevitable anyway.

New plugin builds are required for multiple reasons including new Flatpak runtime, Debian Forky and win64.

That said, I basically agree. On a sidenote they just released 3.3.4 which should be the last release before 3.4. Makes it reasonable safe.

I agree on all above. 3.3.4 (bundled) for all Windows builds, 3.2 for linux/Mac/flatpak.
Let's go in that direction from here.
Are we going to ship 32bit Windows package at all for 5.16? There are no wxWidgets binaries for it for 3.3 anymore, so we would have to build them ourselves.

I have no qualms about declaring O5.16+ is available only as x64 on Windows.
The harder question will eventually become: How long should we continue to update and support plugins for Windows x86? But we do not need to approach that, yet.
We can definitely say that new plugins for Windows will be published for x64 alone. Provides motivation for users to upgrade if they want the new plugin. We might consider pob's rewrite of weather routing to be in this category.

The win32 support for 5.14 exists, so we can probably keep building for it for quite some time, if we want to. And given we now fake win64 support for ABIs 1.18 and newer in opencpn-libs, it should be very simple
Until you need some newer API, which won't be available for win32
And even after that, the "last good" version of the plugin still can be available for old win32 versions

Yes, the "last good" on O5.14 will not be lost.
And we should say that this policy is the "official" word, but does not preclude individual devs from updating x86 plugins for critical issues observed. IOW, if for example I need to fix a bug on o-charts_pi, I may update the x86 build in the catalog if the need is strong enough. I'd rather not, though.
I will of course drop win32 support as soon as it cuses any problem in the CI builds or I need any new API. Until then I will keep it as it "costs nothing"
I have not actually tried an Appveyor x64 build on any plugin. Have you? Just wondering how hard/tedious that might be.
I have win64 builds for dashboardsk now, it was simple. But I build for Windows using Github Actions, abandoned AppVeyor to have to care about one less platform.
Alec's SD template uses Appveyor. SD umbrellas a good number of popular plugins, so simple adaptation of x86 Appveyor script would be the first approach. On my list...
I will do that after the core and opencpn-libs
SD already builds both win32 and win64 using appveyor, thanks to PR from Pavel :)
Yes, but not against wx3.3
OK, that should not be that complicated.
But we first need the core building against it... https://github.com/OpenCPN/OpenCPN/actions/runs/38618547231/job/116039794810?pr=5492
Ah, wxList... you or I?
You have already done plenty, so it's all yours if you have nothing better to do...
I think this a priority, so nothing better to do atm. I'm on it.
Building first round...
... inferior msvc cannot deduce using auto. SIgh.
As we have chainsaws in hands, does VS2026 help with it?
no big deal anyway, just need to explicitly declare the iterator. Not worth the effort for this
